title: Count word frequency
statement: Write a function `wordCount(sentence)` that returns an object showing how many times each word appears. Words are separated by single spaces, and counting ignores case, so `'Go go GO'` gives `{ go: 3 }`. An empty string returns an empty object.
fallbackHints: Imagine tallying words on paper. What would your tally sheet look like, and when would you add a new row?
An object can hold a number for each word, with the word as the key. You will need to split the sentence into separate words and treat upper and lower case the same.

The first time you meet a word it has no entry yet, so reading it gives undefined rather than 0. Think about how to fall back to a default before adding one. Also consider what splitting an empty string gives you.

Create an empty object, lowercase the sentence and split it on spaces, then loop over the words: set each word's count to its previous count (or zero if missing) plus one. Return the empty object early for an empty sentence, then the object at the end.

Use `const counts = {};`, return it early if `sentence === ''`, then `for (const word of sentence.toLowerCase().split(' '))` with `counts[word] = (counts[word] || 0) + 1;`. Finish with `return counts;`.
